<xml xmlns="https://developers.google.com/blockly/xml">
  <block type="arduino_program" x="40" y="40">
    <statement name="SETUP">

      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">13</field><field name="MODE">OUTPUT</field></block>
      </next></block>
    </statement>

        <mutation else="1"></mutation>
        <value name="IF0"><block type="logic_compare"><field name="OP">GT</field>
          <value name="A"><block type="ai_confidence"></block></value>
          <value name="B"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">75</field></shadow></value>
        </block></value>
        <statement name="DO0"><block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">13</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field></statement>
        <statement name="ELSE"><block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">13</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field></statement>
      </block>
    </statement>
  </block>
</xml>

warnings: Inductive Overload Risk (DC Motor fan): DC Motor 'fan' is wired directly to microcontroller GPIO pins. Real physical motors require 200mA–1000mA (MCU pins can only supply 20mA–40mA) and generate inductive back-EMF spikes that damage pins. In physical assembly, use an L298N driver or relay.

warnings: Inductive Overload Risk (DC Motor fan): DC Motor 'fan' is wired directly to microcontroller GPIO pins.         <statement name="ELSE"><block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">13</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field></statement>
      </block>
    </statement>
  </block>
</xml>

instruction.text: Build a Mission 22 · AI Smart Presence Light circuit using Arduino Uno.

target.explanation: Detect a person with Pixiu AI and automatically switch a physical light on only when a person is visible.
target.code:
<xml xmlns="https://developers.google.com/blockly/xml">
  <block type="arduino_program" x="40" y="40">
    <statement name="SETUP">
      <block type="ai_camera_enable"><field name="STATE">ON</field><next>
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">13</field><field name="MODE">OUTPUT</field></block>
      </next></block>
    </statement>
    <statement name="LOOP">
      <block type="controls_if">
        <mutation else="1"></mutation>
        <value name="IF0"><block type="ai_is_detected"><field name="CLASS">person</field></block></value>
        <statement name="DO0"><block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">13</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field></statement>
        <statement name="ELSE"><block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">13</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field></statement>
      </block>
    </statement>
  </block>
</xml>

instruction.text: Build a Mission 11 · MQ-2 Gas & Smoke Sentinel circuit using Arduino Uno.

target.explanation: Detect combustible gas or smoke PPM levels and activate emergency sound and warning strobe.
target.code:
<xml xmlns="https://developers.google.com/blockly/xml">
  <block type="arduino_program" x="40" y="40">
    <statement name="SETUP">
      <block type="serial_begin"><field name="BAUD">9600</field><next>
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">8</field><field name="MODE">OUTPUT</field><next>
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">13</field><field name="MODE">OUTPUT</field></block>
      </next></block></next></block>
    </statement>
    <statement name="LOOP">
      <block type="serial_print"><value name="TEXT"><block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT">Gas PPM: </field></block></value><next>
      <block type="serial_println"><value name="TEXT"><block type="mq2_gas_read"><field name="SENSOR">gas</field></block></value><next>
      <block type="controls_if">
        <mutation else="1"></mutation>
        <value name="IF0">
          <block type="logic_compare">
            <field name="OP">GT</field>
            <value name="A"><block type="mq2_gas_read"><field name="SENSOR">gas</field></block></value>
            <value name="B"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">300</field></shadow></value>
          </block>
        </value>
        <statement name="DO0">
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">8</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">13</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field><next>
          <block type="time_delay"><value name="MS"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">200</field></shadow></value></block>
          </next></block></next></block>
        </statement>
        <statement name="ELSE">
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">8</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">13</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field><next>
          <block type="time_delay"><value name="MS"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">200</field></shadow></value></block>
          </next></block></next></block>
        </statement>
      </block>
      </next></block></next></block>
    </statement>
  </block>
</xml>

instruction.text: Build a ⛅ ESP32 IoT Weather Station & Smartphone Telemetry circuit using ESP32.

target.explanation: Cloud-connected microclimate monitoring station! The ESP32 samples digital temperature and humidity data from DHT11 on GPIO 4 and analog ambient sunlight from an LDR on GPIO 34. Connecting over Virtual Wi-Fi, it hosts a real-time web portal on port 80 that formats and streams live environmental telemetry directly to simulated smartphones, while pulsing the green telemetry TX activity LED on GPIO 2 each time data packets are dispatched.
target.code:
<xml xmlns="https://developers.google.com/blockly/xml">
  <block type="arduino_program" x="40" y="40">
    <statement name="SETUP">
      <block type="serial_begin"><field name="BAUD">115200</field><next>
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">2</field><field name="MODE">OUTPUT</field><next>
      <block type="wifi_connect">
        <value name="SSID"><block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT">SmartHome-WiFi</field></block></value>
        <value name="PASS"><block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT">pixiu123</field></block></value>
        <next>
        <block type="wifi_server_begin">
          <field name="PORT">80</field>
          <next>
          <block type="wifi_server_on">
            <field name="PATH">/</field>
            <statement name="DO">
              <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">2</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field><next>
              <block type="wifi_server_send">
                <field name="STATUS">200</field>
                <field name="TYPE">text/html</field>
                <value name="CONTENT">
                  <block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT"><h1>⛅ ESP32 Cloud Weather</h1><div style="background:#0f172a;padding:12px;border-radius:8px;"><h3 style="color:#38bdf8;">🌡️ Temperature: {{TEMP}}°C</h3><h3 style="color:#22c55e;">💧 Humidity: {{HUMIDITY}}%</h3><h3 style="color:#eab308;">☀️ Ambient Light: {{LUX}} Lux</h3></div><p style="color:#94a3b8;">Live Virtual Wi-Fi telemetry stream active.</p></field></block>
                </value>
                <next>
                <block type="time_delay"><value name="MS"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">150</field></shadow></value><next>
                <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">2</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field></block>
                </next></block>
                </next>
              </block>
              </next></block>
            </statement>
          </block>
          </next></block>
        </next></block>
      </next></block></next></block>
    </statement>
    <statement name="LOOP">
      <block type="time_delay"><value name="MS"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">100</field></shadow></value></block>
    </statement>
  </block>
</xml>

instruction.text: Build a 🔘 Interactive Pushbutton Control Station circuit using Arduino Uno.

instruction.text: How do I set up and wire the 🔢 7-Segment Digital Decade Counter on my Arduino Uno?

target.explanation: Interactive digital decade counter! The Arduino Uno drives all seven segment bars (a-g on pins D2-D8) through common GND to render digits 0 through 9 with glowing LED precision. Each count transition triggers an audio chime on pin D10 and flashes the pulse LED on D13, while an on-canvas Pushbutton on D9 allows manual step increments.

instruction.text: arduino uno 🔢 7-segment digital decade counter wiring

target.explanation: Interactive digital decade counter! The Arduino Uno drives all seven segment bars (a-g on pins D2-D8) through common GND to render digits 0 through 9 with glowing LED precision. Each count transition triggers an audio chime on pin D10 and flashes the pulse LED on D13, while an on-canvas Pushbutton on D9 allows manual step increments.

instruction.text: Build a 🏠 Automated Smart Home circuit using Arduino Uno.

target.explanation: High-voltage home automation with PIR motion and electromechanical relay! The PIR motion sensor monitors room occupancy on digital pin D7. When movement is detected, Arduino energizes an electromechanical relay module on pin D8. The relay's internal electromagnet closes the Normally Open (NO) contacts, routing power from a 9V battery to spin a ceiling cooling fan (DC motor) at 1800 RPM and illuminate the room lamp.

instruction.text: Build a 🐶 BBC micro:bit v2 Virtual Pet & Emotion Companion circuit using micro:bit.

target.explanation: Interactive robotic emotional pet powered by BBC micro:bit v2! The microcontroller boots up by displaying an animated heart icon on its 5x5 LED matrix and centering its servo tail. During the main loop, it shifts between happy and smiling moods, sweeping the servo tail between 45° and 135° on pin P0 while simultaneously pulsing audio chirps on piezo buzzer pin P1 to simulate realistic pet vocalizations.

<xml xmlns="https://developers.google.com/blockly/xml">
  <block type="arduino_program" x="40" y="40">
    <statement name="SETUP">
      <block type="serial_begin"><field name="BAUD">115200</field><next>
      <block type="microbit_show_icon"><field name="ICON">heart</field><next>
      <block type="servo_write"><field name="PIN">0</field><value name="ANGLE"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">90</field></shadow></value></block>
      </next></block></next></block>
    </statement>
    <statement name="LOOP">
      <block type="microbit_show_icon"><field name="ICON">heart</field><next>
      <block type="servo_write"><field name="PIN">0</field><value name="ANGLE"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">135</field></shadow></value><next>
      <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">1</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field><next>
      <block type="time_delay"><value name="MS"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">200</field></shadow></value><next>
      <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">1</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field><next>

      <block type="servo_write"><field name="PIN">0</field><value name="ANGLE"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">45</field></shadow></value><next>
      <block type="time_delay"><value name="MS"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">500</field></shadow></value><next>
      <block type="servo_write"><field name="PIN">0</field><value name="ANGLE"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">90</field></shadow></value><next>
      <block type="time_delay"><value name="MS"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">400</field></shadow></value>

instruction.text: Build a 🌈 NeoPixel 8x RGB Rainbow Audio Visualizer & Mood Lamp circuit using Arduino Uno.

target.explanation: Dynamic sound-and-light disco stage visualizer! An analog potentiometer connected to A0 acts as a tempo and color palette selector.       <block type="neopixel_show"><field name="SENSOR">neo</field></block>
      </next></block></next></block>

      <block type="neopixel_set_color"><field name="SENSOR">neo</field><value name="PIXEL"><block type="math_number"><field name="NUM">0</field></block></value><value name="COLOR"><block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT">#ef4444</field></block></value><next>

instruction.text: Build a 🕹️ Raspberry Pi Pico Retro OLED Arcade Console circuit using Raspberry Pi Pico.

target.explanation: Retro handheld gaming console built on the RP2040 Raspberry Pi Pico! The system initializes a 128×64 SSD1306 OLED over I2C (GP4 SDA / GP5 SCL) displaying game scores. Polling tactile button GP14 detects player fire inputs, instantly updating the OLED with a laser animation, strobing the green blaster LED on GP16, and emitting high-frequency pulse-width audio on GP15 buzzer.
target.code:
<xml xmlns="https://developers.google.com/blockly/xml">
  <block type="arduino_program" x="40" y="40">
    <statement name="SETUP">
      <block type="serial_begin"><field name="BAUD">115200</field><next>
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">14</field><field name="MODE">INPUT</field><next>
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">15</field><field name="MODE">OUTPUT</field><next>
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">16</field><field name="MODE">OUTPUT</field><next>
      <block type="oled_print"><value name="TEXT"><block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT">🎮 PICO ARCADE</field></block></value></block>
      </next></block></next></block></next></block></next></block>
    </statement>
    <statement name="LOOP">
      <block type="controls_if">
        <mutation else="1"></mutation>
        <value name="IF0">
          <block type="io_digitalread"><field name="PIN">14</field></block>
        </value>
        <statement name="DO0">
          <block type="oled_print"><value name="TEXT"><block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT">>> LASER FIRED! <<</field></block></value><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">16</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">15</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field><next>
          <block type="time_delay"><value name="MS"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">120</field></shadow></value><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">15</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">16</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field>
          </block></next></block></next></block></next></block></next></block></next></block>
        </statement>
        <statement name="ELSE">
          <block type="oled_print"><value name="TEXT"><block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT">HI-SCORE: 9850</field></block></value><next>
          <block type="time_delay"><value name="MS"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">200</field></shadow></value>
          </block></next></block>
        </statement>
      </block>
    </statement>
  </block>
</xml>

instruction.text: Build a 📏 Ultrasonic Distance Sensor & 3-Zone Proximity Radar circuit using Arduino Uno.

target.explanation: Automotive 3-zone ultrasonic parking radar with acoustic frequency alarm! The HC-SR04 emits ultrasonic pings from Trig (D9) and Echo (D10) to calculate obstacle distance. Readings stream to Serial Monitor, while three zone LEDs (Green Safe on D13, Yellow Caution on D12, Red Hazard on D11) and Piezo Buzzer D8 provide instant visual and acoustic proximity warnings.
target.code:
<xml xmlns="https://developers.google.com/blockly/xml">
  <block type="arduino_program" x="40" y="40">
    <statement name="SETUP">
      <block type="serial_begin"><field name="BAUD">9600</field><next>
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">8</field><field name="MODE">OUTPUT</field><next>
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">13</field><field name="MODE">OUTPUT</field><next>
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">12</field><field name="MODE">OUTPUT</field><next>
      <block type="io_pinmode"><field name="PIN">11</field><field name="MODE">OUTPUT</field></block>
      </next></block></next></block></next></block></next></block>
    </statement>
    <statement name="LOOP">
      <block type="serial_print"><value name="TEXT"><block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT">Target Distance: </field></block></value><next>
      <block type="serial_print"><value name="TEXT"><block type="ultrasonic_read"><field name="TRIG">9</field><field name="ECHO">10</field></block></value><next>
      <block type="serial_println"><value name="TEXT"><block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT"> cm</field></block></value><next>
      <block type="controls_if">
        <mutation else="1"></mutation>
        <value name="IF0">
          <block type="logic_compare">
            <field name="OP">LT</field>
            <value name="A">
              <block type="ultrasonic_read"><field name="TRIG">9</field><field name="ECHO">10</field></block>
            </value>
            <value name="B">
              <block type="math_number"><field name="NUM">30</field></block>
            </value>
          </block>
        </value>
        <statement name="DO0">
          <block type="serial_println"><value name="TEXT"><block type="text_string"><field name="TEXT">⚠️ DANGER (<30cm): Sounding Alarm!</field></block></value><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">11</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">12</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">13</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">8</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field></block>
          </next></block></next></block></next></block>
          </next></block>
        </statement>
        <statement name="ELSE">
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">11</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">12</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">13</field><field name="STATE">HIGH</field><next>
          <block type="io_digitalwrite"><field name="PIN">8</field><field name="STATE">LOW</field></block>
          </next></block></next></block></next></block>
        </statement>
        <next>
          <block type="time_delay"><value name="MS"><shadow type="math_number"><field name="NUM">400</field></shadow></value></block>
        </next>
      </block>
      </next></block></next></block></next></block>
    </statement>
  </block>
</xml>
